notes: The record of the comparison ASPECT-RASTER already sits at E4 on, written after the fact from artifacts committed at the time.

Aspect is a bearing, so every difference here is a circular separation in 0..180: 359 and 1 are 2 apart, not 358. A plain subtraction would report a false disagreement at the wrap and hide a real one across it.

The comparison runs over the 10,932 interior cells whose slope exceeds 2 degrees. Aspect is undefined on flat ground and the two implementations mark that differently, so including those cells would measure a difference in convention rather than in aspect. The exclusion is part of the frozen protocol, not a filter chosen after the numbers.

The reference was re-run on 2026-07-30 from the command in command.txt, with GDAL 3.13.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gdaldem, and reproduced aspect-gdal.asc byte for byte. The original run recorded its version, platform and command but not its executable path; the path below is the one that reproduced the artifact.

reference.containerPinningNote: No container runtime was used for these references, so no image digest exists to record; the executable path, the reported version, the exact command line and the artifact's own sha256 stand in for it, and the reproduction on 2026-07-30 is what makes that substitution checkable.

datasets.description: The frozen analytic DEM, shared with the slope and hillshade studies rather than copied, so a DEM that drifts invalidates all three at once.
GDAL 3.13.1 Horn aspect in compass degrees on that DEM, the reference side of the comparison.

parameterSets.description: Horn gradient, downslope azimuth as a compass bearing, projected metre grid, one-cell border excluded, cells below 2 degrees of slope excluded because aspect is undefined there.

candidateParameters.outputConvention: compass degrees clockwise from north, downslope

statusReason: All 10,932 compared cells are within the preregistered 0.5 degree circular tolerance, with a maximum separation of 0.000163 degree; GDAL against the closed-form aspect agrees on the same cells.

unsupported: Flat ground. Aspect is undefined below 2 degrees of slope and the two implementations disagree about how to say so: gdaldem writes -9999, or 0 under -zero_for_flat, while this project writes 0 radians in the math frame, which reads as compass 90 and carries no undefined marker.
The one-cell border, which the reference command leaves undefined.

Geographic grids. gdaldem aspect accepts neither -xscale nor -yscale, so an anisotropic aspect reference cannot be produced from the reference tool at all; the matrix run measured a 7.5 degree divergence at latitude 45 with no reference to arbitrate it.
The point-cloud-to-DTM pipeline. This study starts from a DEM.
Accuracy. Two implementations of Horn's method agreeing is not a measurement against ground truth.
